item.content:encoded:
This is an example page. It's different from a blog post because it will stay in one place and will show up in your site navigation (in most themes). Most people start with an About page that introduces them to potential site visitors. It might say something like this:

Hi there! I'm a bike messenger by day, aspiring actor by night, and this is my website. I live in Los Angeles, have a great dog named Jack, and I like piña coladas. (And gettin' caught in the rain.)

...or something like this:

The XYZ Doohickey Company was founded in 1971, and has been providing quality doohickeys to the public ever since. Located in Gotham City, XYZ employs over 2,000 people and does all kinds of awesome things for the Gotham community.

As a new WordPress user, you should go to your dashboard to delete this page and create new pages for your content. Have fun!

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: http://localhost:8898.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

item.title: Blog
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Messaging for Your Business

Communicate Your Core Value Proposition Clearly, Convincingly, and Consistently

A strong idea told authentically can often do more than a multi-million-dollar media buy. Say what you mean in clear, concise, honest language. If you’re promoting a small business with a limited budget, here is a language playbook.

  • Start with a sharp, clear concept. Choose the single message or emotion you want people to feel.
  • Say what you mean, fast. Keep your value proposition sharp, short and obvious.
  • Talk like a human. Honesty, authenticity and clarity beat buzzwords and meaningless catch phrases every time.
  • Be bold enough to be weird. Use this sparingly, the point is, you want to stand out versus blending in.
  • Use what you have. A founder with a smartphone, loyal customers willing to share stories, or recording video in a local setting.
  • Think beyond paid ads. Creative tools like a quiz, a PR stunt or a challenge can cost far less and have a greater impact. Remember with paid advertising you are competing with larger companies with a bigger budget.
  • Test small and fail fast. Run test campaigns, talk to clients. Figure out what works and double down. Lose the things that aren’t working.
  • Keep it honest. Authentic campaigns work if your products and services back up your claims.
  • Emotions beat polish. A rough-cut video with sincerity and a bit of humor trumps a glossy ad no one cares about.
  • Community scales cheaply. Actively participate in communities containing your target audience. Use customers and influencers to tell your story.

item.title: How Much Does it Cost to Market Your Small Business Startup?
item.dc:creator: John
item.content:encoded:
If you only focus on traditional advertising, it can be cost prohibitive unless you have a multi-million dollar Marketing budget. But there are plenty of cost-effective marketing strategies available, like content marketing, social media marketing, street presence and low-cost events.

Establish a Baseline

Let’s say we are just starting our business and the two-year milestone we are targeting is a $500k/yr runrate. According to the US Small Business Administration, The CMO Survey 2025 and other sources, the average spend is 5–10% of revenue or $25-$50k/yr. As a new startup we may, or may not have have that in our budget but it’s always the case that the marketing budget is a limited precious resource that must be put to work and not squandered. How should we plan our Marketing strategy?

Typical Marketing Services Purchased - Based on Industry Assumptions

The table below can be used to give us a general idea as to the types of services we might buy and what they might cost. Before we start planning our actual budget, we need to take several other factors into consideration in order to customize the marketing plan to our actual budget, business goals and most importantly, our target clientele.

*Note: Table generated by claude.ai using the cited data

Paid Acquisition – Google PPC & Social Media Ads

CAUTION: Before pouring money into paid acquisitions, Note: According to Crestmont Capital, The average cost-per-click for high-competition categories like financial, legal, IT Service or security keywords can range from $5–$15 or more. For professional services the conversion rate to Marketing Qualified Lead (MQL) is typically less than 2%. And the rate from MQL to sale is typically between 4-10%. Meaning, at $10/click it will cost you at least $50,000 per sale using paid acquisition.

Unfortunately, I have too often seen organizations squander large portions of their limited budget on paid acquisition without realizing a proper ROI. Before considering PPC and Paid Social media, let's be sure we leverage all our less costly options first.

The key is to focus your efforts on the techniques that will be most effective for your business and target market. Marketing is a long-term game. Sustainable growth comes from consistent effort over time.

Align Your Marketing Projects With Your Business Mission

Defining Your Target Market and Focusing On It, is the Only Winning Strategy in Marketing.

Marketing is about communicating your core value proposition clearly, convincingly, and consistently. It is a critical function that links your organization’s vision and mission to your client base.

The best marketing for small businesses is whatever it takes to reach enough target customers to satisfy your business goals. What this looks like will vary depending on your business, your ideal clientele, your creativity and budget.

There are any number of marketing tools and channels you can choose to deploy but they all take money, time and effort. It’s important to carefully align your limited marketing resources to your business mission and goals.

Seven Steps to Creating Your Marketing Plan

  1. Align with business goals using ROI model
  2. Carefully define your target market
  3. Determine the appropriate communication channels
  4. Define value proposition
  5. Test targeted campaigns
  6. Measure, analyze, adjust; Repeat as necessary
  7. Expand on what works, eliminate what doesn’t

Why Do I Need to Define My Target Market?

Defining your target market and focusing on it, is the only winning strategy in Marketing.

The first step to planning an effective Marketing plan is to carefully identify your target market. Carefully defining your target market and focusing on it is the only winning strategy in marketing. Who are your ideal customers? Where are they physically and online? What need do you fill? What are the alternatives? Who is the competition? What is the best marketing mix to reach them? Etc.

How Can You Measure the ROI of a Marketing Project?

Measure the success of Marketing projects along five levels of buyer journey.

According to The CMO Survey 2025, the most pressing challenge for marketing leaders today is demonstrating the impact of actions on financial outcomes. Managing marketing as a growth engine. is the weakest skill among senior marketing leaders today. There is increasing pressure to ‘prove the value of marketing’. This holds true for all size organizations from very large corporations to small businesses.

According the book ‘ROI in Marketing’, value is embedded in marketing, yet marketers struggle to demonstrate said value at the executive level. Turning marketing from art to science is tricky, nevertheless there are tools we can use to get to an estimate of ROI.

Techniques for Measuring the ROI of Marketing Projects

Consider the buyer journey and results at each of five stages, then, we can both align with business requirements and measure the success of any Marketing initiative.

Measure the success of Marketing projects along five levels of buyer journey;

  1. Customer Reaction
  2. What the Customers Learned
  3. The Actions Customers Took
  4. Financial Impact (purchases)
  5. ROI (profit/cost)

There are a couple outstanding challenges when it comes to measuring the value of Marketing programs. First because so many variables are involved in customer decisions, it is difficult to isolate the effects of the Marketing initiatives. Secondly, it is difficult to translate intangible assets into monetary values. Therefore, most marketers have focused only on impact data for ROI calculations.

Intangible assets are often the key to competitive advantage and organizational success. Intangibles cover strategically important factors behind many well-known organizations’ success.

For Marketers, measuring reaction, learning and action is important. Failure in one of these areas can be measured analyzed and fixed earlier in the life cycle. If your organization has an operational method for monetizing the value of intangible assets you can use that to measure the Marketing results. If not, a simple point-scale method could be used (e.g. 0 – 5 stars).

The point is, using an ROI methodology can help plan to align & measure their projects with respect to your business mission.

Gorilla Marketing

Never underestimate the value of creativity, imagination and out-of-the-box thinking. Guerrilla marketing is an advertisement strategy in which a company uses surprise and/or unconventional interactions in order to promote a product or service. It is a type of publicity. The term was popularized by Jay Conrad Levinson's 1984 (updated 2007) book Guerrilla Marketing. Guerrilla marketing uses multiple techniques and practices to establish direct contact with potential customers. https://a.co/d/04QB7LQh

The key is to focus your efforts on the techniques that will be most effective for your business and target market. Marketing is a long-term game. Sustainable growth comes from consistent effort over time.

Final Thought

Align Marketing strategy to the business goals.

If you are considering hiring a Marketing agency, ask them how they plan to align & measure their projects with respect to the business mission. Are they primarily interested in your success or do they just want to sell you their latest ‘thing’? Do they have a business alignment process?

item.dc:creator: John
item.content:encoded:
Building Credibility & Trust in a Saturated Market

With hundreds or thousands of competitors in your market, buyers are bombarded with similar-sounding solutions — making it extremely difficult for small firms to differentiate themselves. Today’s tech-savvy population has high expectations for digital engagement, making an effective online presence crucial - Your prospective clients demand a high credibility standard — and your website is often the first trust signal.

Budget Constraints vs. High Expectations

Small companies are expected to generate qualified leads with a fraction of the budget larger firms have, pushing toward high-impact, low-cost strategies like email marketing, SEO, social media and direct outreach.

You’ve got to spread your limited Marketing budget across channels in order to effectively reach your target audience. Business is all about people and your most valuable marketing activities are in-person, online live events or one-on-one video meetings. You can’t blow your annual marketing on an agency developing your website.

Yet, according to Column Five Media, a website redesign that wins over both executives and technical evaluators costs $15,000 to $75,000, with the option to keep an agency involved for ongoing marketing support at $10k/yr. That can be pricey for a startup. Luckily, lower-cost solutions that are equally competitive, if not more so, are available.

See my blog “How to Publish a Competitive Professional Services Website for $60.”

Messaging

Organizations must simplify messaging without dumbing down, speaking to business impact rather than features — explaining how a solution enables client productivity and supports growth.

In today’s AI driven search model, the key to SEO messaging is to clearly explain what you do and the client benefits of your solution in a manner tightly focused on your target market. Messaging should be clear, authentic, personal, credible and professional. The biggest digital marketing expense in terms of time and money is content creation. AI tools, agencies and freelancers can help save time gathering data and creating rough drafts, but final publication should reflect your authentic personality and expertise.

1.Procure WordPress Subscription & Domain Name

WordPress offers five different subscription levels. This technique will work on all of them but for purposes of this money-saving demo, I’m using the Personal Subscription model which is the least expensive, yet has everything you need for this project. At the time of this writing, it cost $48 for the first year including hosted site and domain name registration. You can then register your DNS domain name.

2.Step Two – Setup a Blank Site & Install UpsideNowBasic

Download the UpsideNowBasic Theme .zip file and accompanying content.xml file from the WordPress Market or directly from GitHub.

Once you have your domain, you can go ahead and use WordPress to create a blank site. Once the site is up, click on the Appearance – Themes tab and click on ‘Install new theme’. Upload the upsidenowbasic.zip file and click ‘Install Now’. After installation is completed, go to the Appearance – Themes tab and activate UpsideNowBasic.

Next go to the Tools – Import tab and install the WordPress Importer. Click on ‘Run Importer’ and browse to the content.xml file. Then click ‘Upload file and import’. You now have an internet ready theme and 4-page website layout and are ready for customization and adding your content.

3.Step Three – Customize Theme for Your Brand

Click on the Appearance – Editor – Styles tab and browse through the customization features. UpsideNowBasic has pre-installed a set of popular Google fonts and includes a curated collection of color palettes. Not to worry if you change your mind later, I’m certain you will. You can swap out design elements at a click, which propagates across your site. (NOTE: It’s always best to make customizations at the highest level possible and avoid too many page-level .html customizations in terms of colors and fonts or other elements you want to be consistent across your site.)

4.Step Four – Add Content & Publish

Use the block editor tools, add your content and publish your site.

5.Step Five (optional) – Google SEO Performance Metrics & Security Check

There are various tools available to analyze your SEO, site performance and security.

item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Privacy Policy

When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day. See the Cookie Policy page for details.

Embedded content from other websites

Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

How long we retain your data

If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.
